extracted.intended_audience: agency rulemaking participants (regulated entities, attorneys, aviation industry, and interested public)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements appearing in a Federal Register issue covering agency rulemaking, airworthiness directives, airspace designation, instrument approach procedures, petitions/interventions, and related notice-and-comment deadlines. Useful for regulated parties and members of the public participating in or complying with federal rulemaking and administrative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to participate in rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons have been afforded an opportunity to participate in the making of the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide interested persons an opportunity to submit comments/views on proposed amendments; the publication records whether such opportunity was provided and whether comments were considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor corrections may bypass notice-and-comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Since this correction is minor in nature, notice and public procedure hereon are unnecessary and the amendment may be made effective immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an amendment/ correction is characterized as 'minor', agencies may forgo further notice and public procedure and adopt the change with immediate effect. The agency must explain why the change is minor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified comment periods for proposed regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties were given 45 days after publication in which to submit written data or views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal Register text shows different prescribed comment windows (examples include 30 days, 45 days depending on the proposal). Agencies should state the length of the comment period in the proposal and note when comments were received (e.g., 'All comments received were favorable').

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-cause exception for expedited effective dates
rubrics_metrics.description: As a situation exists which demands immediate action in the interests of safety in air commerce, I find that compliance with the notice and procedure provisions of the Administrative Procedure Act is impracticable and that good cause exists for making this amendment effective within less than 30 days from publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For safety-critical matters (e.g., instrument procedures, airworthiness directives), agencies may invoke 'good cause' to shorten or waive the usual notice period and make rules effective immediately; the agency must state the safety justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and compliance timeframe for airworthiness directives
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance required within the next 100 hours' time in service after the effective date of this AD unless already accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Airworthiness directives specify a clear compliance window (e.g., hours in service, calendar date) and reference the required service bulletin or procedure to be followed for corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means of identification chosen for practical inspectability
rubrics_metrics.description: The color of the fan blades was used as a means of identification since all affected fan blades are aluminum colored and it is necessary only to remove the front cover of the unit to inspect the fan blade. Since the serial number placards are located on the lower aft side, most installations would require the removal of the unit from the bulkhead in order to check the serial number. Therefore, no change has been made in the AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing identification criteria (serial number vs visible attribute), agencies may prefer the method that allows easier inspection and compliance in the field; motivation and practical considerations should be documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and unit conventions for instrument approach procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Bearings, headings, courses and radials are magnetic. Elevations and altitudes are in feet MSL. Ceilings are in feet above airport elevation. Distances are in nautical miles unless otherwise indicated, except visibilities which are in statute miles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrument approach procedures must use standardized units and conventions; agencies republish full procedures using these conventions and indicate changes for clarity and uniformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Republishing complete procedures when amended
rubrics_metrics.description: For the convenience of the users, the complete procedure is republished in this amendment indicating the changes to the existing procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When instrument approach procedures are amended, the agency republishes the entire procedure (not just the changes) so users have a self-contained, updated text showing amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard content and minima for approach procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If an instrument approach procedure of the above type is conducted at the below named airport, it shall be in accordance with the following instrument approach procedure... Initial approaches shall be made over specified routes. Minimum altitudes shall correspond with those established for en route operation in the particular area or as set forth below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach procedures must provide initial approach routes, course/distance, minimum altitudes, transition and ceiling/visibility minima, and exceptions/notes; these form the standard criteria for safe execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/administrative deadlines and citation of procedural rules for interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of intervention or petitions to intervene may be filed with the Federal Power Commission, Washington, D.C., in accordance with the rules of practice and procedure (18 CFR 1.8 and 1.37 (f)) on or before February 15, 1966.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must state intervention filing deadlines and cite the governing CFR rules so interested parties know how and when to file petitions to intervene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions for reconsideration postpone effective date and require particularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested person may file a petition seeking reconsideration of the following numbered proceedings within 20 days from the date of publication of this notice. Pursuant to section 17(b) of the Interstate Commerce Act, the filing of such a petition will postpone the effective date of the order in that proceeding pending its disposition. The matters relied upon by petitioners must be specified in their petitions with particularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions for reconsideration must be filed within the prescribed short window (example: 20 days), must specify grounds with particularity, and will stay the order's effective date while pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protests to applications must follow prescribed rules and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Protests to the granting of an application must be prepared in accordance with Rule 1.40 of the general rules of practice (49 CFR 1.40) and filed within 15 days from the date of publication of this notice in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where statute or Commission practice requires protests, the notice will cite the exact procedural rule and the filing deadline (example: 15 days); protests must conform to the specified rule format and content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission may suspend proposed rate changes pending hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplement No. 9 to Southland's FPC Gas Rate Schedule No. 14 is conditionally accepted for filing, and is hereby suspended and the use thereof deferred until February 20, 1966, and thereafter until such further time as it is made effective in the manner prescribed by the Natural Gas Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a proposed rate change raises questions of lawfulness (unjust, unreasonable, discriminatory), the Commission can order a hearing and suspend the proposed change's effectiveness pending disposition; the notice will set the suspension date and instructions for intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to waive statutory notice requirements absent good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Southland requests that its proposed rate increase be permitted to become effective as of August 20, 1965. Good cause has not been shown for waiving the 30-day notice requirement provided in section 4(d) of the Natural Gas Act to permit an earlier effective date for Southland’s rate filing and such request is denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to waive statutory notice periods (e.g., 30-day notice under Natural Gas Act) are disfavored unless the filer demonstrates good cause; agency will explicitly grant or deny such waiver requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for ordering a hearing on filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed changed rate and charge may be unjust, unreasonable, unduly discriminatory, or preferential, or otherwise unlawful. The Commission finds it is necessary and proper in the public interest ... that the Commission enter upon a hearing concerning the lawfulness of the proposed change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the agency determines that a filing might be unlawful or injurious to the public interest, it will order a hearing; the notice explains the public interest rationale and procedural next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: No restriction on republication of Federal Register material
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no restrictions on the republication of material appearing in the Federal Register or the Code of Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material published in the Federal Register/CFR may be republished without restriction; the notice clarifies distribution/ republication rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized notices for distribution and subscriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution to the public is made only by the Superintendent of Documents, Government Printing Office ... The Weekly Compilation of Presidential Documents will be furnished by mail to subscribers for $6.00 per year, payable to the Superintendent of Documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal publications state official distribution channels, subscription pricing, and ordering instructions; users must follow the stated procedures to receive official copies.
